claim: RNAi-mediated depletion of splicing factors results in mitotic abnormalities.
source: Several studies have shown that RNAi-mediated depletion of splicing factors (SFs) results in mitotic abnormalities.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and is stated as an established finding in the literature.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 are required for chromosome segregation in both Drosophila and human cells.
source: Here, we show that two highly conserved SFs, Sf3A2 and Prp31, are required for chromosome segregation in both Drosophila and human cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Injections of anti-Sf3A2 and anti-Prp31 antibodies into Drosophila embryos disrupt mitotic division within 1 min.
source: Injections of anti-Sf3A2 and anti-Prp31 antibodies into Drosophila embryos disrupt mitotic division within 1 min, arguing strongly against a splicing-related mitotic function of these factors.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from embryo injection experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: The rapid disruption of mitotic division by antibody injection argues strongly against a splicing-related mitotic function of Sf3A2 and Prp31.
source: Injections of anti-Sf3A2 and anti-Prp31 antibodies into Drosophila embryos disrupt mitotic division within 1 min, arguing strongly against a splicing-related mitotic function of these factors.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the rapid timing of the phenotype, which is inconsistent with the time required for splicing and translation.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 bind spindle microtubules.
source: We demonstrate that both SFs bind spindle microtubules (MTs) and the Ndc80 complex, which in Sf3A2- and Prp31-depleted cells is not tightly associated with the kinetochores
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data including immunofluorescence and in vitro microtubule co-sedimentation assays.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 bind the Ndc80 complex.
source: We demonstrate that both SFs bind spindle microtubules (MTs) and the Ndc80 complex, which in Sf3A2- and Prp31-depleted cells is not tightly associated with the kinetochores
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP and GST pulldown experiments showing physical interactions.

claim: In Sf3A2- and Prp31-depleted cells, the Ndc80 complex is not tightly associated with the kinetochores.
source: We demonstrate that both SFs bind spindle microtubules (MTs) and the Ndc80 complex, which in Sf3A2- and Prp31-depleted cells is not tightly associated with the kinetochores
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing reduced Ndc80 accumulation at kinetochores in SF-depleted cells.

claim: In HeLa cells, the Ndc80/HEC1-SF interaction is restricted to the M phase.
source: in HeLa cells the Ndc80/HEC1-SF interaction is restricted to the M phase.
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP experiments from synchronized HeLa cells showing interaction only in mitotic cells.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 directly regulate interactions among kinetochores, spindle microtubules and the Ndc80 complex in both Drosophila and human cells.
source: These results indicate that Sf3A2 and Prp31 directly regulate interactions among kinetochores, spindle microtubules and the Ndc80 complex in both Drosophila and human cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental results including binding assays, localization studies, and phenotypic analyses.

claim: RNAi against Sf3A2 or Prp31 results in abnormal chromosome congression and segregation in Drosophila S2 cells.
source: We have previously observed that RNAi against the Drosophila homologues of SF3A2 (CG10754; henceforth designated Sf3A2) and PRPF31 (CG6876; henceforth Prp31) results in abnormal chromosome congression and segregation (Somma et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work and is confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 are both found in the Drosophila spliceosomal B complex.
source: Sf3A2 and Prp31 are both found in the Drosophila spliceosomal B complex and interact with the U2 and U4/U6 snRNPs, respectively (Herold et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work on spliceosome composition.

claim: Sf3A2 interacts with the U2 snRNP.
source: Sf3A2 and Prp31 are both found in the Drosophila spliceosomal B complex and interact with the U2 and U4/U6 snRNPs, respectively (Herold et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work on spliceosome composition.

claim: Prp31 interacts with the U4/U6 snRNPs.
source: Sf3A2 and Prp31 are both found in the Drosophila spliceosomal B complex and interact with the U2 and U4/U6 snRNPs, respectively (Herold et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work on spliceosome composition.

claim: RNAi against Sf3A2 or Prp31 strongly reduces the levels of these proteins in S2 cells.
source: western blotting of cell extracts demonstrated that these antibodies specifically recognize bands of the expected molecular weights (33 and 65 kDa, respectively), and that these bands are strongly reduced after RNAi against the corresponding genes (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data showing reduced protein levels after RNAi treatment.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells show significant increases in monopolar spindles compared to mock controls.
source: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells showed similar mitotic phenotypes; they exhibited significant increases in both monopolar spindles and PMLES as compared to mock controls.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative cytological analysis data presented in Figure 1D.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells show significant increases in PMLES (prometaphase-like cells with elongated spindles) compared to mock controls.
source: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells showed similar mitotic phenotypes; they exhibited significant increases in both monopolar spindles and PMLES as compared to mock controls.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative cytological analysis data presented in Figure 1D.

claim: PMLES are prometaphase-like cells with elongated spindles associated with chromosomes comprising both sister chromatids.
source: PMLES are peculiar prometaphase-like cells with elongated spindles associated with chromosomes comprising both sister chromatids (Figure 1B and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images showing the morphology of PMLES.

claim: Some PMLES show central spindle-like structures and irregular cytokinetic rings while still possessing elevated Cyclin B levels.
source: Intriguingly, some PMLES showed central spindle-like structures and irregular cytokinetic rings, while still possessing elevated Cyclin B levels (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing Cyclin B, central spindle markers, and cytokinetic ring markers in PMLES.

claim: PMLES show kinetochore-associated BubR1, a SAC protein that normally dissociates from kinetochores at the metaphase-anaphase transition.
source: they also showed kinetochore-associated BubR1, a SAC protein that normally dissociates from kinetochores at the metaphase-anaphase transition (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing BubR1 localization in PMLES.

claim: PMLES are metabolically in a pre-anaphase stage but are nevertheless permissive of typical telophase events.
source: PMLES are therefore metabolically in a pre-anaphase stage but are nevertheless permissive of typical telophase events, such as central spindle assembly and initiation of cytokinesis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that PMLES have high Cyclin B and BubR1 at kinetochores (pre-anaphase markers) but also show central spindle and cytokinetic ring formation (telophase events).

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells show a higher frequency of pre-anaphase mitotic figures and a lower frequency of ana-telophases compared to controls.
source: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells showed a higher frequency of pre-anaphase mitotic figures (prometaphases, metaphases and PMLES) and a lower frequency of ana-telophases compared to controls, suggesting that they suffer of a substantial delay in the metaphase-to-anaphase transition.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data on mitotic stage frequencies presented in Figure 1D.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells suffer a substantial delay in the metaphase-to-anaphase transition.
source: Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells showed a higher frequency of pre-anaphase mitotic figures (prometaphases, metaphases and PMLES) and a lower frequency of ana-telophases compared to controls, suggesting that they suffer of a substantial delay in the metaphase-to-anaphase transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the altered frequencies of mitotic stages observed in RNAi cells.

claim: PMLES are a consequence of defective kinetochore-MT interaction in S2 cells.
source: We have previously observed frequent PMLES (formerly called pseudo-ana-telophases, abbreviated as PATs; Somma et al., 2008) in S2 cells depleted of the centromere-specific histone H3 Cid/Cenp-A or the kinetochore components Ndc80, Nuf2 and Kmn1/Nsl1 (Renda et al., 2017; Somma et al., 2008), suggesting that PMLES are a consequence of a defective kinetochore-MT interaction in S2 cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that PMLES occur in cells depleted of various kinetochore components.

claim: dsRNAs targeting the 5' UTR of Sf3A2 or the 3' UTR of Prp31 produce the same mitotic phenotypes as dsRNAs directed to the coding sequences.
source: dsRNAs targeting the 5' UTR of Sf3A2 or the 3' UTR of Prp31 produced the same mitotic phenotypes as the dsRNAs directed to the coding sequences
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data on mitotic phenotypes shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The mitotic phenotypes caused by Sf3A2 or Prp31 RNAi are rescued by expression of RNAi resistant genes lacking the UTRs.
source: these phenotypes were rescued by expression of RNAi resistant genes (Sf3A2-RFP and Prp31-GFP) lacking the UTRs (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), ruling out the possibility of RNAi off-target effects.
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data showing restoration of normal mitotic phenotypes.

claim: The rescue experiments rule out the possibility of RNAi off-target effects.
source: these phenotypes were rescued by expression of RNAi resistant genes (Sf3A2-RFP and Prp31-GFP) lacking the UTRs (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), ruling out the possibility of RNAi off-target effects.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the rescue experiment results.

claim: In mock-treated control S2 cells, all mitotic divisions entered anaphase within 45 min after prometaphase/metaphase.
source: We imaged 14 mitotic divisions of mock-treated control cells. All of them entered anaphase within 45 min after prometaphase/metaphase (P/M), namely, the time when the chromosomes are already fully condensed and begin to align to form the metaphase plate (Figure 2, Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging data from control cells.

claim: Of 35 Sf3A2-depleted dividing cells analyzed, only two entered anaphase within 45 min after P/M.
source: In contrast, of 35 Sf3A2-depleted dividing cells analyzed, only two entered anaphase within 45 min after P/M, two more displayed a delayed anaphase initiation (54 min and 1 hr 22 min after P/M) accompanied by defective chromosome segregation, while the other 31 cells examined remained in a metaphase-like stage with unseparated sister chromatids for the entire time of filming, which ranged from 1 hr 30 min to more than 4 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging data from Sf3A2 RNAi cells.

claim: Most Sf3A2-depleted cells remain in a metaphase-like stage with unseparated sister chromatids for extended periods (1 hr 30 min to more than 4 hr).
source: In contrast, of 35 Sf3A2-depleted dividing cells analyzed, only two entered anaphase within 45 min after P/M, two more displayed a delayed anaphase initiation (54 min and 1 hr 22 min after P/M) accompanied by defective chromosome segregation, while the other 31 cells examined remained in a metaphase-like stage with unseparated sister chromatids for the entire time of filming, which ranged from 1 hr 30 min to more than 4 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging data from Sf3A2 RNAi cells.

claim: In about one third of Sf3A2-depleted cells that remain in metaphase-like stage, the chromosomes remain at the center of the cell.
source: In about one third of these cells, the chromosomes remained at the center of the cell; in the other two thirds, the chromosomes exhibited oscillations, dispersing along the spindle and within the cytoplasm (Figure 2, Video 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging observations.

claim: In about two thirds of Sf3A2-depleted cells that remain in metaphase-like stage, the chromosomes exhibit oscillations, dispersing along the spindle and within the cytoplasm.
source: In about one third of these cells, the chromosomes remained at the center of the cell; in the other two thirds, the chromosomes exhibited oscillations, dispersing along the spindle and within the cytoplasm (Figure 2, Video 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging observations.

claim: The phenotype of Prp31-depleted cells is similar to that seen in Sf3A2 RNAi cells in live-cell imaging.
source: The phenotype of Prp31-depleted cells was similar to that seen in Sf3A2 RNAi cells. We filmed 12 cells; three entered anaphase after 40, 50 or 85 min after P/M; the other 9 cells examined remained in a metaphase-like stage for the entire time of filming, which ranged from 1 hr 50 min to 3 hr 50 min (Figure 2, Video 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging data from Prp31 RNAi cells.

claim: RNAi against Sf3A2 or Prp31 in larval brains results in irregularly shaped spindles and increased monopolar figures.
source: In Sf3A2-RNAi brains, the spindles were often irregularly shaped; 25% of the cells were monopolar and the frequency of ana-telophases was lower than in controls (15% vs 31%). A similar phenotype was observed in Prp31 RNAi brains, which displayed a substantial increase in monopolar figures and a decrease in ana-telophases compared to controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytological analysis of larval brain cells.

claim: Clear PMLES figures similar to those seen in S2 cells were not observed in Sf3A2- or Prp31-depleted brain cells.
source: However, in brains we did not observe clear PMLES figures similar to those seen in Sf3A2- or Prp31-depleted S2 cells, suggesting that brain cells possess a control mechanism that prevents spindle elongation in the absence of chromosome segregation and Cyclin B degradation.
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of PMLES in brain cell observations.

claim: Brain cells possess a control mechanism that prevents spindle elongation in the absence of chromosome segregation and Cyclin B degradation.
source: However, in brains we did not observe clear PMLES figures similar to those seen in Sf3A2- or Prp31-depleted S2 cells, suggesting that brain cells possess a control mechanism that prevents spindle elongation in the absence of chromosome segregation and Cyclin B degradation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the difference in phenotypes between S2 cells and brain cells.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 form subcomplexes with specific interacting partners.
source: Studies on splicing factors have shown that both Sf3A2 and Prp31 form subcomplexes with specific interacting partners (Herold et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies on spliceosome structure.

claim: RNAi against Sf3A1, Sf3A3/noisette, Prp3, Prp4/U4-U6-60K, Prp6/CG6841, Prp8, and hoip/CG3949 did not reveal obvious mitotic defects.
source: To ask whether the components of these subcomplexes are involved in mitosis, we performed RNAi against Sf3A1 and Sf3A3/noisette that encode Sf3A2 interactors, and against Prp3, Prp4/U4-U6-60K, Prp6/CG6841, Prp8 and hoip/CG3949, the genes that specify the Drosophila homologues of Prp31 interactors. The cytological analysis of these RNAi cells did not reveal obvious mitotic defects (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytological analysis data showing normal mitotic phenotypes.

claim: Only individual subunits of the spliceosome subcomplexes, and not the entire subcomplexes, are specifically required for mitosis.
source: Nonetheless, considering that RNAi against Sf3A2 or Prp31 strongly reduces the levels of the corresponding proteins, we believe that at least some of the Sf3A2- and Prp31-interacting factors do not play mitotic roles. This suggests that only individual subunits of the spliceosome subcomplexes, and not the entire subcomplexes, are specifically required for mitosis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that RNAi against interacting partners does not produce mitotic phenotypes.

claim: In Sf3A2-depleted cells, the SAC is not satisfied.
source: These results indicate that in Sf3A2-depleted cells the SAC is not satisfied and this is at least in part responsible for the observed phenotype.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that disruption of the SAC machinery partially rescues the phenotype.

claim: Disruption of the SAC machinery by Sf3A2 zw10 double RNAi allows more cells to enter anaphase compared to Sf3A2 RNAi alone.
source: As shown in Figure 1D, Sf3A2 zw10 double RNAi cells displayed a three-fold decrease in the frequency of PMLES and an almost two-fold increase in the frequency of ana-telophases compared to cells depleted of Sf3A2 only.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from double RNAi experiments.

claim: The time from NEB to initial chromosome alignment is similar between control-injected and α-Sf3A2- or α-Prp31-injected embryos.
source: In movies starting just before NEB, the time elapsing from NEB to initial chromosome alignment was similar between control-injected and α-Sf3A2- or α-Prp31-injected embryos.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative timing data from live embryo imaging.

claim: The length of metaphase is significantly increased in embryos treated with anti-Sf3A2 or anti-Prp31 antibodies.
source: However, the length of metaphase was significantly increased in embryos treated with the anti-SF antibodies (Figure 4A and B, Videos 4–6).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative timing data from live embryo imaging showing statistical significance.

claim: In α-Sf3A2- and α-Prp31-injected embryos, spindles do not increase to mature metaphase spindle length but remain 'stunted'.
source: In addition, in both α-Sf3A2- and α-Prp31-injected embryos, spindles did not increase to mature metaphase spindle length, as occurred with controls, but remained 'stunted'.
evidence: The claim is supported by spindle length measurements from live embryo imaging.

claim: The decrease in spindle length in anti-SF injected embryos becomes significant at 64 s following NEB and remains significant until anaphase.
source: This decrease in spindle length relative to controls became significant at 64 s following NEB and remained significant until anaphase (Figure 4A and C, Videos 5 and 6)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative spindle length measurements over time with statistical analysis.

claim: 20 s prior to anaphase onset, the spindles of anti-SF injected embryos are approximately 30% shorter than those of controls.
source: such that, 20 s prior to anaphase onset, the spindles of anti-SF injected embryos were approximately 30% shorter than those of controls (Figure 4A and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative spindle length measurements.

claim: The chromosomes of α-Sf3A2- and α-Prp31-injected embryos are less aligned than in controls throughout the extended metaphase period.
source: Our qualitative observations also suggested that the chromosomes of α-Sf3A2- and α-Prp31-injected embryos were less aligned than in controls throughout the extended metaphase period (Figure 4A, Videos 5 and 6). To test this, we measured the area encompassed by the chromosomes during the last 80 s (20 frames) that precede anaphase in anti-SF injected embryos. The chromosomes were indeed less tightly aligned than in their mock-injected counterparts (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements of chromosome alignment area.

claim: Anti-SF injected embryos show a complete failure in chromosome segregation during anaphase, such that chromosomes decondense and coalesce in a single indistinct mass.
source: Finally, the most striking defect in anti-SF injected embryos was a complete failure in chromosome segregation during anaphase, such that chromosomes decondensed and coalesced in a single indistinct mass (Figure 4A, Videos 5 and 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging observations of chromosome behavior.

claim: The spindle length phenotype in anti-SF injected embryos manifests within 110 s following injection.
source: In this case, NEB occurs 16 s after the movie begins. As it takes 15–30 s to begin filming following injection, we can unequivocally conclude that the spindle length phenotype manifests within 110 s (30 + 16 + 64) following injection.
evidence: The claim is based on calculation from timing data of injection, filming start, and phenotype appearance.

claim: Embryos injected with anti-SF antibodies during late telophase do not exhibit an increase in the length of the following S phase compared to mock-injected control nuclei.
source: Embryos injected with either of the SF antibodies during late telophase did not exhibit an increase in the length of the following S phase compared to the mock-injected control nuclei, suggesting interphase/S phase was not disrupted.
evidence: The claim is supported by timing measurements from live embryo imaging.

claim: Embryos injected with anti-SF antibodies during late telophase display the same mitotic defects when they enter mitosis as embryos injected just before or during mitosis.
source: However, when these embryos entered mitosis they displayed the same defects seen in embryos injected just before or during mitosis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of phenotypes across different injection timings.

claim: Embryos in metaphase immediately following injection with α-Sf3A2 or α-Prp31 antibodies manifest the same phenotype as those injected during interphase.
source: Further, embryos which were in metaphase immediately following injection with α-Sf3A2 or α-Prp31 antibodies manifested the same phenotype as those injected during interphase – with short spindles, poorly aligned chromosomes and failure in segregation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of phenotypes across different injection timings.

claim: The mitotic phenotype observed upon anti-SF injection occurs in less than 1 min.
source: As no more than 30 s elapsed between injection and the start of imaging, and the short spindle phenotype was clear since the beginning of filming (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), we conclude that the mitotic phenotype observed upon anti-SF injection occurs in less than 1 min.
evidence: The claim is based on timing calculations from injection and imaging data.

claim: Embryos injected with anti-Dgt6 antibodies show delayed spindle formation, thinner and long spindles, and arrest in a metaphase-like state.
source: Consistent with previous results (Hayward et al., 2014), the embryos injected with the anti-Dgt6 antibodies showed delayed spindle formation, thinner and long spindles and arrested in a metaphase-like state.
evidence: The claim is supported by live embryo imaging data and citation to previous work.

claim: The phenotype elicited by anti-Dgt6 antibodies is very different from that elicited by anti-SF antibodies.
source: This phenotype is very different from that elicited by anti SF-antibodies, ruling out the possibility that the mitotic effects of the anti-SF antibodies are due to chemical contaminants associated with antibody purification and concentration processes.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of phenotypes and serves as a control for antibody specificity.

claim: Fluorescently labeled α-Sf3A2 and α-Prp31 antibodies are virtually excluded from interphase and prophase nuclei in live syncytial embryos.
source: Both antibodies were virtually excluded from interphase and prophase nuclei.
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging of fluorescently labeled antibodies.

claim: As soon as the nuclear envelope becomes fenestrated and the spindle is formed, the anti-SF antibodies quickly penetrate into the nuclear space and remain there until anaphase.
source: However, as soon as the nuclear envelope became fenestrated and the spindle was formed, the antibodies quickly penetrated into the nuclear space and remained there until anaphase
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging of fluorescently labeled antibodies showing their localization dynamics.

claim: During interphase, the anti-SF antibodies cannot disrupt the splicing process that occurs within the nucleus.
source: These results strongly suggest that during interphase the antibodies cannot disrupt the splicing process that occurs within the nucleus.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that antibodies are excluded from interphase nuclei.

claim: Even if anti-SF antibodies are injected one minute before nuclear fenestration, they can act on kinetochores/microtubules only after their entry into the nucleus at prometaphase.
source: Additionally, even if the antibodies are injected one minute before nuclear fenestration, they can act on kinetochores/microtubules only after their entry into the nucleus at prometaphase.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the antibody localization dynamics and nuclear envelope structure.

claim: Splicing does not occur during mitosis.
source: Thus, given that splicing does not occur during mitosis (Hofmann et al., 2010; Shin and Manley, 2002), our embryo injection experiments make highly unlikely an indirect, splicing-dependent mitotic effect of Sf3A3 and Prp31 inhibition.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies on transcription and splicing during mitosis.

claim: During interphase and prophase, both Sf3A2 and Prp31 are strongly enriched in the nucleus in S2 cells.
source: During interphase and prophase both Sf3A2 and Prp31 were strongly enriched into the nucleus, as expected for SFs
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing nuclear localization.

claim: In prometaphase S2 cells, both Sf3A2 and Prp31 show a diffuse distribution.
source: in prometaphase cells both SFs showed a diffuse distribution (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: In metaphase S2 cells with tightly aligned chromosomes, both Sf3A2 and Prp31 are enriched in the central part of the spindle but excluded from the spindle poles and the asters.
source: However, in metaphase figures with tightly aligned chromosomes, both Sf3A2 and Prp31 were enriched in the central part of the spindle but excluded from the spindle poles and the asters (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing specific spindle localization.

claim: During anaphase in S2 cells, Sf3A2 and Prp31 localize at the center of the dividing cells.
source: During anaphase, Sf3A2 and Prp31 localized at the center of the dividing cells
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: In telophase S2 cells, Sf3A2 and Prp31 are not bound to spindle but accumulate into the reforming nuclei.
source: while in telophase cells they were not bound to spindle but accumulated into the reforming nuclei.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: S2 cells depleted of Sf3A2 or Prp31 do not show any spindle staining after incubation with the pertinent antibody.
source: Cells depleted of Sf3A2 or Prp31 did not show any spindle staining after incubation with the pertinent antibody (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data demonstrating antibody specificity.

claim: Sf3A2-RFP and Prp31-GFP are enriched in metaphase spindles of S2 cells.
source: To obtain additional evidence for localization of the SFs in the spindle we examined cells expressing Sf3A2-RFP or Prp31-GFP under the control of the actin promoter, and found an enrichment of the tagged proteins in the metaphase spindles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy of tagged proteins.

claim: After colchicine treatment, both Sf3A2 and Prp31 are diffuse and do not show any enrichment in any spindle-like structure in S2 cells.
source: We found that after this treatment both Sf3A2 and Prp31 are diffuse and do not show any enrichment in any spindle-like structure (i. e. the spindle matrix).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from colchicine-treated cells.

claim: RNAse-treated metaphases display normal spindle staining with anti-Sf3A2 and anti-Prp31 antibodies.
source: In contrast, RNAse-treated metaphases displayed a normal spindle staining with anti-Sf3A2 and anti-Prp31 antibodies (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from RNAse-treated cells.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 associate with spindle MTs during metaphase and this association is not mediated by RNA molecules.
source: Thus, Sf3A2 and Prp31 associate with spindle MTs during metaphase and this association is not mediated by RNA molecules.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the colchicine and RNAse treatment results.

claim: Over 80% of either 6His-Sf3A2 or 6His-Prp31 co-sediments with 2 μM taxol-stabilized MTs.
source: We found that, while neither SF was present in the pellet fraction in the presence of unpolymerized tubulin, over 80% of either 6His-Sf3A2 or 6His-Prp31 co-sediments with 2 μM taxol-stabilized MTs (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro MT co-sedimentation assay data.

claim: Neither 6His-Sf3A2 nor 6His-Prp31 is present in the pellet fraction in the presence of unpolymerized tubulin.
source: We found that, while neither SF was present in the pellet fraction in the presence of unpolymerized tubulin, over 80% of either 6His-Sf3A2 or 6His-Prp31 co-sediments with 2 μM taxol-stabilized MTs (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro MT co-sedimentation assay data showing specificity for polymerized MTs.

claim: Increasing NaCl concentration from 50 to 200 mM strongly reduces MT binding of 6His-Sf3A2 and 6His-Prp31.
source: Furthermore, increasing NaCl concentration from 50 to 200 mM strongly reduced MT binding of 6His-Sf3A2 or 6His-Prp31, demonstrating that the MT-SF interaction is based on ionic attraction (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by salt-dependent MT binding assay data.

claim: The MT-SF interaction is based on ionic attraction.
source: Furthermore, increasing NaCl concentration from 50 to 200 mM strongly reduced MT binding of 6His-Sf3A2 or 6His-Prp31, demonstrating that the MT-SF interaction is based on ionic attraction (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the salt sensitivity of the MT-SF interaction.

claim: The mouse orthologue of Sf3A2 binds MTs.
source: These in vitro results, coupled with the finding that the mouse orthologue of Sf3A2 binds MTs (Takenaka et al., 2004), provide a biochemical basis to support the conclusion that Sf3A2 and Prp31 associate with the MTs of metaphase spindles.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work on the mouse protein.

claim: TMT quantitative proteomic analysis identified 4483 protein IDs in control S2 cells.
source: This quantitative proteomic analysis identified 4483 protein IDs in control S2 cells (the full dataset can be found at www.thewakefieldlab/ms).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Prp31 was the most reduced protein in Prp31 RNAi cell extracts in the proteomic analysis.
source: Prp31 was the most reduced protein in Prp31 RNAi cell extracts, while Sf3A2 was the second most reduced protein in Sf3A2 RNAi cell extracts, demonstrating the validity of the comparative mass spectrometry (MS) approach (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data demonstrating RNAi efficiency.

claim: Sf3A2 was the second most reduced protein in Sf3A2 RNAi cell extracts in the proteomic analysis.
source: Prp31 was the most reduced protein in Prp31 RNAi cell extracts, while Sf3A2 was the second most reduced protein in Sf3A2 RNAi cell extracts, demonstrating the validity of the comparative mass spectrometry (MS) approach (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data demonstrating RNAi efficiency.

claim: Knock down of Prp31 and Sf3A2 has a less general effect on splicing than Sf3A1.
source: Interestingly, Sf3A1 RNAi resulted in 948 proteins significantly reduced, suggesting knock down of Prp31 and Sf3A2 has a less general effect on splicing than Sf3A1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of the number of proteins reduced in different RNAi conditions.

claim: Only a single protein, HUS1-like, is significantly reduced in both Prp31 and Sf3A2, but not Sf3A1, RNAi cells among proteins with mitotic GO terms.
source: Figure 6 shows a Venn diagram, comparing these IDs for each RNAi condition. Only a single protein, HUS1-like, is significantly reduced in both Prp31 and Sf3A2, but not Sf3A1, RNAi cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by GO term analysis of the proteomic data.

claim: HUS1-like is involved in homologous recombination repair during meiosis.
source: As HUS1-like is involved in homologous recombination repair during meiosis (Peretz et al., 2009), it is unlikely to be the causative factor in the SF phenotype observed in S2 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work on HUS1-like function.

claim: There is no evidence that the mitotic phenotypes seen upon Prp31 or Sf3A2 RNAi in S2 cells are a result of reduced protein levels caused by defective splicing.
source: Thus, we conclude there is no evidence that the mitotic phenotypes seen upon Prp31 or Sf3A2 RNAi in S2 cells are a result of reduced protein levels, caused by defective splicing.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the proteomic analysis results.

claim: Loss of Sf3A2 or Prp31 does not affect the localization of Cid, Cenp-C, Mis12, Kmn1, AurB, BubR1, or Zw10 in S2 cells.
source: Indirect immunofluorescence of S2 cells depleted of either SF via RNAi, showed that loss of either protein does not affect the localization of Cid, Cenp-C, Mis12, Kmn1, AurB, BubR1, or Zw10 (Figure 1C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing normal localization of these proteins.

claim: Sf3A2 or Prp31 depletion strongly reduces kinetochore localization of Ndc80 and Spc25/Mitch in S2 cells.
source: However, Sf3A2 or Prp31 depletion strongly reduced kinetochore localization of Ndc80 and Spc25/Mitch (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing reduced kinetochore signals.

claim: The reduction in kinetochore-localized Ndc80 in SF-depleted cells is not due to a reduction in the Ndc80 protein level.
source: Crucially, this effect was not due to a reduction in the Ndc80 protein, as western blotting showed no significant difference in the Ndc80 levels between control and Sf3A2 or Prp3 RNAi cell extracts, consistent with our proteomic analyses (Figure 6, Supplementary file 1), Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot and proteomic data showing normal Ndc80 protein levels.

claim: Colchicine-treated Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells display the same levels of Ndc80 at kinetochores as colchicinized control cells.
source: Moreover, the kinetochores of colchicine-treated (for 3 hr) Sf3A2 and Prp3 RNAi cell displayed the same levels of Ndc80 as colchicinized control cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from colchicine-treated cells.

claim: Ndc80 association with kinetochores of SF-depleted cells is destabilized in the presence of spindle MTs.
source: This finding suggests that Ndc80 association with kinetochores of SF-depleted cells is destabilized in the presence of the spindle MTs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Ndc80 localization is normal in colchicine-treated SF-depleted cells but reduced in untreated SF-depleted cells.

claim: Mitch accumulation at kinetochores is substantially reduced in Sf3A2 and Prp31 RNAi cells not treated with colchicine, but not in RNAi cells exposed to the drug.
source: Comparable results were obtained with Spc25/Mitch. Mitch accumulation at kinetochores was substantially reduced in Sf3A2 and Prp3 RNAi cells not treated with colchicine, but not in RNAi cells exposed to the drug (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data comparing untreated and colchicine-treated cells.

claim: Each splicing factor (Sf3A2 and Prp31) interacts in vivo with both Ndc80 and Nuf2.
source: Reciprocal Co-IP assays showed that each splicing factor interacts in vivo with both Ndc80 and Nuf2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP experimental data.

claim: GST-Ndc80, GST-Nuf2 and GST-Mitch efficiently precipitate 3HA-Sf3A2 and 3HA-Prp31 from S2 cell extracts.
source: These results were confirmed by GST pulldown experiments from S2 cells extracts expressing 3HA-Sf3A2 or 3HA-Prp31; we found that GST-Ndc80, GST-Nuf2 and GST-Mitch efficiently precipitate 3HA-Sf3A2 and 3HA-Prp31 (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pulldown experimental data.

claim: Both 6His-Sf3A2 and 6His-Prp31 efficiently bind GST-tagged components of the Ndc80 complex (GST-Ndc80, GST-Nuf2, GST-Mitch) but not GST alone.
source: Both 6His-Sf3A2 and 6His-Prp31 efficiently bound the GST-tagged components of the Ndc80 complex but not GST alone (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pulldown experiments with purified proteins demonstrating direct binding.

claim: Both 6His-Sf3A2 and 6His-Prp31 fail to bind the Drosophila telomeric proteins HOAP and Ver.
source: To check for a non-specific protein-binding activity of the His-tagged SFs we tested whether they bind two GST-tagged proteins functionally unrelated with kinetochores; we found that both SFs fail to bind the Drosophila telomeric proteins HOAP (HP1/ORC-associated protein) and Ver (Verrocchio) (Raffa et al., 2011), arguing against the possibility of nonspecific interactions between the SFs and the Ndc80 complex (Figure 7—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by negative control GST pulldown experiments.

claim: Sf3A2 and Prp31 interact with each other.
source: Finally, given that Sf3A2 and Prp31 bind the same kinetochore components, we asked whether they interact with each other. Reciprocal Co-IP experiments from S2 cell extracts clearly showed that they co-purify (Figure 7F).
evidence: The claim is supported by reciprocal Co-IP experimental data.

claim: Ndc80 RNAi cells show many PMLES and a reduced frequency of ana-telophases, similar to SF-depleted cells.
source: Fixed Ndc80 RNAi cells showed many PMLES (26%) and a reduced frequency of ana-telophases just like the SF-depleted cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative cytological analysis comparing Ndc80 RNAi to SF RNAi phenotypes.

claim: Ndc80 RNAi cells exhibit ana-telophase-like figures with decondensed chromosomes that are not stained by Cyclin B or BubR1 and show unequal chromosome segregation.
source: However, in addition to PMLES, Ndc80 RNAi cells also exhibited ana-telophase-like figures with decondensed chromosomes. These latter figures were not stained by either Cyclin B or BubR1 and almost invariably showed unequal chromosome segregation (Figure 8B, C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from Ndc80 RNAi cells.

claim: In Ndc80-depleted cells filmed live, after approximately 90 min of chromosome oscillations, chromosomes start to decondense as normally occurs at the end of telophase.
source: However, after approximately 90 min of oscillations, chromosomes started to decondense as normally occurs at the end of telophase (Figure 8E, Video 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging data from Ndc80 RNAi cells.

claim: A similar chromosome decondensation process was not observed in cells depleted of either Sf3A2 or Prp31.
source: A similar chromosome decondensation process was not observed in cells depleted of either Sf3A2 or Prp31.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of live-cell imaging data between Ndc80 RNAi and SF RNAi cells.

claim: Overexpression of Ndc80-TAP at low levels does not alter the mitotic phenotypes observed after Sf3A2 or Prp31 depletion.
source: Cytological analysis showed that Ndc80-TAP expression at low level does not alter the mitotic phenotypes observed after Sf3A2 or Prp31 depletion (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytological analysis of cells with induced Ndc80 expression.

claim: High expression levels of Ndc80-TAP slightly increase the frequencies of ana-telophases but do not affect the PMLES frequencies in SF-depleted cells.
source: High expression levels of Ndc80-TAP slightly increased the frequencies of ana-telophases but did not affect the PMLES frequencies (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytological analysis of cells with high induced Ndc80 expression.

claim: The mitotic phenotypes elicited by RNAi against the SFs are largely independent of the intracellular levels of Ndc80.
source: These results indicate that the mitotic phenotypes elicited by RNAi against the SFs are largely independent of the intracellular levels of Ndc80.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Ndc80 overexpression does not rescue the SF RNAi phenotype.

claim: The localization of human SF3A2 and PRP31 in HeLa cells is similar to that seen in Drosophila S2 cells.
source: We first determined the localization of these proteins by immunostaining dividing HeLa cells with antibodies directed to the human orthologues of Sf3A2 and Prp31. This localization was similar to that seen in Drosophila S2 cells (see Figure 5A, Figure 9, Figure 9—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of immunofluorescence data from HeLa and S2 cells.

claim: In HeLa metaphases with tightly aligned chromosomes, SF3A2 and PRP31 are associated with the central part of the spindle.
source: the human SFs were present in the nucleus during interphase, while in metaphases with tightly aligned chromosomes they were associated with the central part of the spindle.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from HeLa cells.

claim: Brief nocodazole treatments lead to diffuse localization of SF3A2 and PRP31 in HeLa metaphase cells.
source: Brief nocodazole treatments led to a diffuse localization of the SFs in metaphase cells, suggesting that they associate with the spindle and not with the spindle matrix, consistent with the results obtained in S2 cells (Figure 9A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from nocodazole-treated HeLa cells.

claim: Loss of either SF3A2 or PRP31 in HeLa cells results in morphologically irregular spindles, reduced frequency of metaphases with congressed chromosomes, frequent monopolar spindles, and low frequency of ana-telophases.
source: Loss of either SF3A2 or PRP31 resulted in a virtually identical mitotic phenotype, comparable to that observed in Drosophila cells depleted of the homologous SFs. We observed cells with morphologically irregular spindles, a strong reduction in the normal frequency of metaphases with congressed chromosomes, frequent monopolar spindles, and a low frequency of ana-telophases (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytological analysis of SF-depleted HeLa cells.

claim: The mitotic phenotypes in SF-depleted HeLa cells are rescued by ectopic expression of FLAG-tagged SF3A2 or PRP31 genes bearing siRNA-resistant mutations.
source: These phenotypes were rescued by the ectopic expression of FLAG-tagged SF3A2 or PRP31 genes bearing translationally silent mutations that render them insensitive to the siRNAs (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data in HeLa cells.

claim: In SF3A2 and PRP31 depleted HeLa cells not treated with nocodazole, HEC1 accumulation at kinetochores is reduced without a concomitant significant reduction in the amount of the protein.
source: Consistent with the results in Drosophila, HEC1 accumulation at the kinetochores was reduced, without a concomitant significant reduction in the amount of the protein (Figure 9B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence and Western blot data from HeLa cells.

claim: In most SF-depleted HeLa cells, there is a halo of HEC1 in the cytoplasmic area surrounding the chromosomes.
source: We specifically observed that in most RNAi cells there was a halo of HEC1 in the cytoplasmic area surrounding the chromosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence observations.

claim: The HEC1 halo fluorescence is significantly more intense in SF RNAi HeLa cells than in control cells.
source: We measured the fluorescence of this halo in prometaphase cells, and found that it was significantly more intense in RNAi cells than in control cells (Figure 9D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence measurements with statistical analysis.

claim: SF3A2 and PRP31 RNAi HeLa cells treated with nocodazole display HEC1 signals comparable to those of control cells.
source: SF3A2 and PRP31 RNAi cells treated with nocodazole (for 3 hr) displayed HEC1 signals comparable to those of control cells and most of them did not show a fluorescent HEC1 halo around the chromosomes (Figure 9E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from nocodazole-treated HeLa cells.

claim: Both SF3A2 and PRP31 physically interact with each other in HeLa cells.
source: Consistent with the Drosophila results, we found that both SFs physically interact with each other and with HEC1 (Figure 10A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP experimental data from HeLa cells.

claim: Both SF3A2 and PRP31 physically interact with HEC1 in HeLa cells.
source: Consistent with the Drosophila results, we found that both SFs physically interact with each other and with HEC1 (Figure 10A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP experimental data from HeLa cells.

claim: Anti-HEC1 antibody fails to precipitate SF3A2 or PRP31 from HeLa cells in S phase or G2 phase.
source: The anti-HEC1 antibody failed to precipitate either SF3A2 or PRP31 from cells in the S phase (time 0) or in the G2 phase (5 hr after release of the block), but efficiently pulled down both SFs from dividing cells expressing the mitotic marker phospho-histone H3 (PHH3) (Goto et al., 1999) 8 hr after release from the block (Figure 10C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP data from synchronized HeLa cells at different cell cycle stages.

claim: Anti-HEC1 antibody efficiently pulls down both SF3A2 and PRP31 from dividing HeLa cells expressing the mitotic marker phospho-histone H3.
source: The anti-HEC1 antibody failed to precipitate either SF3A2 or PRP31 from cells in the S phase (time 0) or in the G2 phase (5 hr after release of the block), but efficiently pulled down both SFs from dividing cells expressing the mitotic marker phospho-histone H3 (PHH3) (Goto et al., 1999) 8 hr after release from the block (Figure 10C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP data from synchronized HeLa cells.

claim: SF3A2 and PRP31 do not interact with HEC1 in mitotic HeLa cells with depolymerized MTs (collected at 0 hr after nocodazole removal).
source: Co-IP with an anti-HEC1 antibody did not detect any HEC1-SF interaction in cells shaken-off from nocodazole-containing cultures or from adherent cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP data from nocodazole-synchronized HeLa cells.

claim: Mitotic HeLa cells collected 6 hr after nocodazole removal display a robust interaction between HEC1 and either SF3A2 or PRP31.
source: However, mitotic cells shaken off from cultures kept in fresh medium for 6 hr after nocodazole removal displayed a robust interaction between HEC1 and either SF3A2 or PRP31.
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP data from nocodazole-synchronized HeLa cells after recovery.

claim: The physical interaction between HEC1 and either SF3A2 or PRP31 is restricted to mitosis.
source: These results indicate that the physical interaction between HEC1 and either SF3A2 or PRP31 is restricted to mitosis, when pre-mRNA splicing is suppressed (Hofmann et al., 2010; Shin and Manley, 2002) and kinetochore proteins and SFs can come into contact following nuclear envelope breakdown.
evidence: The claim is inferred from Co-IP data showing interaction only in mitotic cells.

claim: The HEC1-SF interaction does not occur in mitotic cells with depolymerized MTs but takes place when these cells have reassembled a spindle.
source: The finding that this interaction does not occur in mitotic cells with depolymerized MTs, but takes place when these cells have reassembled a spindle, further suggests that the HEC1-SF interaction requires the presence of the spindle MTs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from Co-IP data comparing nocodazole-treated and recovered cells.

claim: In SF3A2- or PRP31-depleted HeLa cells fixed after Triton X-100 pre-extraction, HEC1 is associated with filaments that appear to protrude from CREST-stained kinetochores.
source: In contrast to control cells, in which HEC1 staining was confined to kinetochores, in SF3A2- or PRP31-depleted mitotic cells, we found HEC1 associated with filaments that in many cases appear to protrude from the CREST-stained kinetochores (Figure 11A)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from pre-extracted cells.

claim: The HEC1 filaments observed in SF3A2 and PRP31-depleted HeLa cells are stained by anti-tubulin antibodies, suggesting they are kinetochore fibers.
source: these filaments were also stained by anti-tubulin antibodies, suggesting that they are kinetochore fibers (Figure 11B).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization of HEC1 and tubulin signals in immunofluorescence.

claim: The HEC1 filaments observed in SF3A2 and PRP31-depleted HeLa cells are enriched in HURP.
source: We also stained Triton X-100 pre-extracted cells with antibodies against HURP, which localizes predominantly to the kinetochore fibers (Silljé et al., 2006) and found that the HEC1 filaments observed in SF3A2 and PRP31-depleted cells are enriched in HURP (Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization of HEC1 and HURP signals in immunofluorescence.

claim: SF3A2 and PRP31 interact with Ndc80/HEC1 on the k-fibers, regulating the association of the Ndc80 complex with the kinetochore.
source: We propose that these SFs interact with Ndc80/HEC1 on the k-fibers, regulating the association of the Ndc80 complex with the kinetochore.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on inference from multiple experimental observations.

claim: In the absence of SF3A2 and PRP31, the Ndc80/HEC1 complex would associate with the kinetochores in an abnormal fashion, weakening the binding and preventing SAC satisfaction.
source: In the absence of the SFs, the Ndc80/HEC1 complex would associate with the kinetochores, or the kinetochore-MT interfaces, in an abnormal fashion, so that the binding of the complex to the kinetochore would be weakened and the SAC satisfaction prevented.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: When kinetochores are attached to MTs in SF-depleted cells, Ndc80/HEC1 would diffuse away from the kinetochores possibly along the kinetochore fibers.
source: As a result, when the kinetochores are attached to MTs, Ndc80/HEC1 would diffuse away from the kinetochores possibly along the kinetochore fibers.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on inference from experimental observations.
